scope.surface: Sidebar inline search rows, highlight semantics, selection, query clearing, and runtime readiness

productLoss: The first same-snapshot Browser pair rendered Web's dedicated 36px search-result rows but reused Lynx's complete 82px thread rows and 91px cards.
The Lynx result path had no dedicated selected-row anatomy, so the query state retained status/card content instead of the compact title, favicon, and time layout.

The selected model mutation attached its rejection callback as the second argument to then; Lynx reported a recovered SocketOpenError through its global Promise channel. The mutation now ends in an explicit catch without changing optimistic rollback semantics.
harnessMismatch: The first after capture rendered the correct dedicated rows, but the workbench still measured legacy data-thread-id cards. Measurement now prefers data-sidebar-search-result rows.

Lynx CDP serializes id as idSelector and did not reliably return HostList aria-label attributes. Runtime evidence therefore uses option-row role and aria-selected semantics while source tests lock the listbox contract.

Two running-session model-switch verification attempts did not reach product assertions: one failed with EADDRNOTAVAIL on an ephemeral local socket and one lost its temporary DevTool device. They remain harness loss and do not overwrite the successful idle-thread recovery evidence.
Physical keyboard focus, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter, and Escape remain pending-user-session. The Native query probe is explicitly not represented as keyboard input.
classification.evidenceBoundary: Browser before and after share one immutable snapshot, Web bundle, route, query, theme, viewport, result identities, and zero-error console. Browser supplies direct product pixels. Exact-bundle Native separately proves two 36px option rows, first-row highlight, a real DevTool tap on the second result, active-thread mutation, query clearing, row dismissal, main sequence advance, zero renderer errors, and isolated cleanup.
